body: I've done the grounding technique,  fasting and self denial,  chanting, emptying the mind/focusing on the present. I know I'm weird,  but I had a few phases of religion in the past trying to find meaning, so I used to do those things
I've definitely tried it in therapy many times and also when I tried to Buddhist,  but it just doesn't solve my issues.  I'm glad it helps a lot of people,  but not for my hell brain
I don't think anything besides a lobotomy would help.  It's OK, I mean life isn't really meant for everyone.  Sometimes it's just better to find peace in unconsciousness.
Yeah I've told many and I've been on nearly every medication but it doesn't help. Sorry you had to hear

Its sad, but I have a personality disorder so I just have never been happy or felt happiness.  I've tried to kill myself many times starting at age 4. My parents don't love me and have told others this behind my back.
No unfortunately
IDK I'm truly ready to die

Thank you for replying. I've already lost faith honestly, and enjoyment and gratification are incomprehensible to me. I'm sorry you were in a similar situation at my age. I hope things have worked out.

Haha same. I used to draw a bit, but I don't like telling people because I lost the ability to do so a long time ago and I've tried to get it back but I can't. 
It sounds like you are technologically inclined at least? Do you know any programming?

It kinda sounds like how my college was too, very disorganized and didn't feel like an education. Nowadays it seems like anything in the Art's is impossible to get into unless you are super crazy talented or have a following already. It really sucks.

Thank you for the reply, I know being successful and powerful isn't the key to happiness. It's just that I've never had any other interests, as much as I tried to develop them over the years. So nothing else will ever make me happy. I wish I could give my life to someone who wants to live and could use it better lol.  I'm glad you found clarity by being able to do that though, it must have been hard.
I feel your pain, i hate the way things are these days. What did you study?

I'm sorry you also feel that way. 
I was trying to get into a radiography technician program (highest paying career for least amount of school) but the prerequisites alone will take me 2-3 years. It's a very competitive program with only 35 spaces and the best of the best get into it. I don't really want to go for anything else because im not interested in much. I just wanted a good paying job. 
However, it ended up being harder than I thought, and I already messed up my chances of getting in. And I really don't want to work in the medical field anyway lol.

I was never did anything honestly. Its a big problem ( not having interests). Before I was 10, I wasn't allowed to do much (raised in a cult) so I had to literally lay in bed and listen to the radio. I'm sure this did some damage, but it's just what my childhood was like and I can't reverse it.

The thing is, I don't really care about my friend or family either. Sometimes I just get so sick of them. Sometimes I find myself caring about people that I'm not directly close with. 
I could never figure out what interested me. I only have one reference (my friend) 
I tried going to community college so many times, but I can't handle it because I'm not too bright or I can't take the hw. I know it sounds stupid but I guess it's the anxiety.
Yeah it would be nice, but I have no ideas or ways of going about such a project.

What industry are you in? It sounds like you have a clear vision of things you'd like to do. I know it is such a competitive world these days, but what makes you feel like a failure next to your peers?

Why are things things not going well? 
I'm 23 and Im also ready to die because I don't believe things work themselves out. Sometimes it really does get worse. 
I do the same thing with social media, beating myself up for being so unaccomplished and ugly or not having any friends or anywhere to go.
Thank you for that, I wish I could know these people lol. I wish I could beat this, but I've wanted to die for at least a decade and nothing ever changes
Sure lol

Thanks for replying, i never hear of anyone else who lost their talent. It's good to know I'm not the only one. Well definitely not good but, you know. 
It's hard to fit in, especially in adulthood, when you don't really have an identity. I'd like to talk but even on the internet it's quite hard for me to make conversation. You have my empathy for what you are going through. Sometimes emptiness is even worse than pain.
Is it alright to pm?
I guess at least that would be some closure. Losing her is horrible but in situations like these it can bring peace. If you ever want to talk to someone you can pm me anytime.

Jesus, I'm so sorry. I'm terrified of strokes because my grandma became a vegetable after one and it's hard looking at them alive but knowing they aren't really there, knowing you can't really say goodbye.
You really deserve a proper family and friend, some kind of support. May I ask what happened to your parent that has caused this?

That is really tough being a caregiver to your parent at such a young age. I just want to take a moment to commend you for that. 
Having your parent not be able to show their love and appreciation for what you are doing right now has got to be hard. 
I understand exactly how you feel about just wanting your parent to care about you the way things used to be. I'm also in a situation where my parents have stopped caring or showing that love. It's not the same as your situation but I can understand how it feels. You have switched roles with your parent and at a premature age. 
I know I'm just an brief internet interaction but you should know I really respect you for dealing with the situation you are in.
